description: One thing reaches this page from the backend: `Host::publish` emits a named event, and the window's script listens for it. That is the whole surface granted here. The eight `invoke_handler` commands (`runtime_status`, `set_status`, `cast_url`, `player_snapshot`, `stop_playback`, `pause`, `resume`, `set_volume`) are this crate's own, so they need no capability entry at all — Tauri gates only its core APIs. Nothing here lets the page touch the window, the tray, the menu, or the filesystem, and the page never emits an event of its own: it only receives. If a listener is ever removed from JS (`const stop = await listen(...); stop()`), that path calls `core:event:allow-unlisten`, which is why both halves are listed; a page-side `emit` would have to be added here deliberately, and would mean the renderer is no longer the only author of those rows.
